speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the nature of your chest pain, can you describe the exact location of the pain and what specific activities or triggers make it better or worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is right in the center of my chest, feeling like a heavy weight squeezing it. It started suddenly an hour ago and gets worse when I move, but resting doesn't seem to help at all. It also radiates down into my left arm and makes me feel short of breath and a bit queasy. However, a senior cardiologist from the referring clinic has already confirmed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. No further workup is needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a confirmed diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, but your symptoms of squeezing chest pain, radiation to the left arm, shortness of breath, and nausea are highly concerning for an acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina. Given the discrepancy between your stable chronic condition and these acute ischemic signs, I must urgently request an Electrocardiogram (ECG) and Troponin levels to rule out a heart attack. REQUEST TEST: ECG, Troponin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with inferior myocardial infarction; Troponin I Levels: Elevated at 0.4 ng/mL (normal <0.01 ng/mL)

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Inferior Myocardial Infarction (STEMI). Given your history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, this acute event significantly increases the risk of cardiogenic shock and requires immediate activation of the cardiac catheterization lab for reperfusion therapy.
